messages:
maya.p: heads up — we're seeing a bunch of SDK questions about what to do when clients hit 429s for per-route limits. main asks: which headers are guaranteed, how to surface bucket info to callers, and how to stay backward-compatible with older SDKs that expect just Retry-After.

kevin: nice. do we have a single contract doc? iirc we added Rate-Limit, Rate-Limit-Bucket, and Quota-Info headers in the new spec but kept Retry-After for backcompat.

sam: correct — servers will still send Retry-After for TTL-based 429s. new fields are optional hints: `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Bucket` (opaque id), `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset` (unix sec), and `X-Redwood-Quota-Snapshot` (json-blob string). older SDKs should ignore unknown headers.

maya.p: question from integration team — if we send both Retry-After and Reset, which should the SDK prefer? and what's the recommended client fallback when only a bucket id is present?

frank: prefer explicit Reset when present because Retry-After can be relative and sometimes set by infra proxies. Reset is absolute unix time so it's deterministic. SDKs: use Reset -> Retry-After delta -> exponential backoff default. if only bucket id present, it's a soft-signal: treat as a low-severity hint (do light backoff, e.g., 250ms * attempts) and surface a warning to the app.

kevin: +1. also recommend emitting metrics from SDK: rate_limit.hints.received and rate_limit.bucket.<id>.soft_hits so customers can see pattern.

sam: note about `X-Redwood-Quota-Snapshot`: it may contain small JSON like `{"limit":1000,"used":987,"window":3600}` encoded as a header value. SDKs must parse gracefully and ignore if it's malformed.

maya.p: could we add a tiny pseudocode snippet for the SDK team to copy?

frank: sure — paste into thread, keep short:

```
// preferred order
if (header.Reset) wait = max(0, header.Reset - now)
else if (header.RetryAfter) wait = parseInt(header.RetryAfter)
else if (header.RateLimitRemaining == '0' && header.Bucket) wait = heuristicBackoff(attempts)
else wait = jitteredExponential(attempts)
```

kevin: FYI for backcompat: older SDKs that only look at Retry-After will still work; proxies will continue to set Retry-After for normal rate limits. only case to watch is quota-snapshot driven soft 429s where Retry-After may be absent — so we should ensure server adds Retry-After when we require strict client pause.

sam: ops note: we're planning to roll this out as a gradual change next week behind a feature flag `rl-hints-v2`. when enabled infra will emit the new headers for selected routes.

maya.p: perfect. can SDK owners add parsing for Quota-Snapshot safe-parse + metric and a short log message when bucket-only 429 occurs? i can open a tiny PR with suggested tests.

kevin: please do. suggested test cases: (1) header Reset present (2) Retry-After only (3) bucket-only + malformed snapshot (4) valid snapshot with numeric fields.

frank: add a typeless tolerant parser e.g. `JSON.parseSafe(header['X-Redwood-Quota-Snapshot'])` -> map numbers or strings to Number when possible. fallback values: limit=null, used=null, window=null.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rl-hints-v2 -> canary on eng-runtime at 2026-03-18T02:00Z :rocket:

maya.p: thanks all — i'll draft the PR/wiki blurb and ping SDK leads. tagging @kevin @sam for reviews. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks! quick note — add one-line to CHANGELOG about header names and backcompat expectations.

sam: and maybe an example curl response snippet for docs. e.g.:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Bucket: rwd-abc123
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 1712349999
X-Redwood-Quota-Snapshot: {"limit":1000,"used":1000,"window":3600}
```

maya.p: great, i'll include that. closing thread after PR opened.
